Exodus 1: Israel's descendants are enslaved in Egypt and build the store cities Pithom and Raamses (Exodus 1:11). The Bible's own count places the exodus about 1446 BC (1 Kings 6:1), though some scholars prefer the 1200s BC.
Exodus 2: Moses is born in Egypt, raised in Pharaoh's household, and flees to Midian, east of the Gulf of Aqaba, where he lives for many years (Exodus 2:23).
Exodus 3: Moses is tending Jethro's flock at Horeb, "the mountain of God" (Exodus 3:1). He is about eighty when he returns to Egypt (Exodus 7:7).
Exodus 4: Moses returns from Midian to Egypt with his wife and sons; Aaron meets him at the mountain of God.
Exodus 5: Moses and Aaron go before Pharaoh in Egypt, soon after Moses returns from Midian. Moses is about eighty years old (Exodus 7:7).
Exodus 6: Moses is still in Egypt, just after his first meeting with Pharaoh has made the slaves' work harder (Exodus 5:22–23).
Exodus 7: Moses is eighty and Aaron eighty-three (Exodus 7:7). The first plague strikes the Nile, Egypt's only source of water and farmland.
Exodus 8: The plagues continue in Egypt. Moses meets Pharaoh by the river in the morning (Exodus 8:20), while Israel lives apart in the land of Goshen (Exodus 8:22).
Exodus 9: Plagues strike livestock, bring boils, and send hail when "the flax and the barley was smitten" (Exodus 9:31), placing it in late winter or early spring.
Exodus 10: Still in Egypt, after the hail has ruined the flax and the barley (Exodus 9:31), Moses and Aaron go back to Pharaoh's court.
Exodus 11: Moses stands before Pharaoh for the last time, just before the first Passover in the month Abib (Exodus 12:2; Exodus 13:4).
Exodus 12: Passover is set in the month Abib, the first month of the year (Exodus 12:2; 13:4). Israel leaves Rameses for Succoth after 430 years in Egypt (Exodus 12:40–41).
Exodus 13: Israel travels from Succoth to Etham, "in the edge of the wilderness" (Exodus 13:20), avoiding the coastal road through Philistine land.
Exodus 14: Israel camps at Pihahiroth "between Migdol and the sea" (Exodus 14:2). The Hebrew name for the sea, yam suph, means ‘sea of reeds.’
Exodus 15: After the crossing, Israel travels three days into the wilderness of Shur to Marah, then to Elim with its twelve wells and seventy palm trees.
Exodus 16: Israel reaches the wilderness of Sin on the fifteenth day of the second month (Exodus 16:1). Manna begins and continues for forty years.
Exodus 17: Israel camps at Rephidim, near Horeb, the last stop before Mount Sinai (Exodus 17:1, 6; Exodus 19:2).
Exodus 18: Jethro, priest of Midian, brings Moses' wife and sons to the camp "at the mount of God" (Exodus 18:5).
Exodus 19: Israel reaches the wilderness of Sinai in the third month after leaving Egypt (Exodus 19:1). The traditional site is Jebel Musa in the southern Sinai Peninsula.
Exodus 20: Israel is camped at the foot of Mount Sinai in the third month after leaving Egypt (Exodus 19:1–2).
Exodus 21: Laws given at Sinai begin with slaves, injuries, and property, written as cases—"if a man…"—like other ancient Near Eastern law codes such as Hammurabi's (about 1750 BC).
Exodus 22: At Mount Sinai, right after the Ten Commandments, Moses stands near the thick darkness where God is (Exodus 20:21) and receives these laws.
Exodus 23: Still at Mount Sinai, God gives laws for the day Israel will live in Canaan and gather for feasts each year.
Exodus 24: Moses writes the words of the covenant, builds an altar with twelve pillars, and goes up the mountain for forty days and nights (Exodus 24:18).
Exodus 25: Moses is on top of Mount Sinai, inside the cloud, for forty days and forty nights (Exodus 24:18).
Exodus 26: Still on the mountain, Moses receives the plan for a tent that a people on the move can take down and carry.
Exodus 27: Instructions follow for the bronze altar and the courtyard, 100 cubits by 50 (about 150 by 75 feet).
Exodus 28: Moses is on Mount Sinai for forty days (Exodus 24:18), while Aaron, who will wear these garments, waits in the camp below (Exodus 24:14).
Exodus 29: On the mountain, Moses learns the ceremony he will carry out once the tabernacle is finished (Leviticus 8).
Exodus 30: Moses is still on Mount Sinai, near the end of his forty days in the cloud (Exodus 24:18).
Exodus 31: At the end of Moses' forty days on Mount Sinai (Exodus 24:18), God gives him the two tables of testimony (Exodus 31:18).
Exodus 32: While Moses is on the mountain, the people make a golden calf at its foot. Bull images were associated with gods in Egypt and Canaan.
Exodus 33: Moses pitches a tent outside the camp, "the Tabernacle of the congregation" (Exodus 33:7), where he meets with God.
Exodus 34: Moses cuts two new stone tables and spends another forty days on the mountain (Exodus 34:28).
Exodus 35: Moses gathers the people in the camp at the foot of Mount Sinai, after the covenant is renewed in chapter 34.
Exodus 36: The building begins in the camp below Mount Sinai, soon after Moses comes down with the new tablets (Exodus 34:29).
Exodus 37: Work continues in the camp below Mount Sinai in the months before the tabernacle is set up (Exodus 40:17).
Exodus 38: The courtyard is finished in the camp at Sinai, near the end of Israel's first year out of Egypt.
Exodus 39: The work is finished at Sinai, within a year of Israel's arrival there (Exodus 19:1; Exodus 40:17).
Exodus 40: The tabernacle is set up "on the first day of the first month" of the second year (Exodus 40:17), almost a year after leaving Egypt.
Leviticus 1: Israel is still camped at Sinai. God speaks to Moses "out of the tabernacle of the congregation" (Leviticus 1:1), which had just been set up (Exodus 40).
Leviticus 2: At Sinai, Moses receives the rules for meat (grain) offerings.
Leviticus 3: At Sinai, Moses receives the rules for peace offerings.
Leviticus 4: At Sinai, Moses receives the rules for sin offerings.
Leviticus 5: At Sinai, Moses receives the rules for trespass offerings.
Leviticus 6: At Sinai, the priests receive instructions for handling each offering.
Leviticus 7: The offering laws given at Sinai conclude (Leviticus 7:37–38).
Leviticus 8: Aaron and his sons are consecrated as priests over seven days at the tabernacle door.
Leviticus 9: On the eighth day, Aaron offers the first sacrifices, and fire comes out from before the LORD.
Leviticus 10: It is the same day the priests begin serving at the tabernacle, in the camp at Sinai (Leviticus 9:1; Leviticus 10:19).
Leviticus 11: At Sinai, Israel receives laws on clean and unclean animals.
Leviticus 12: At Sinai, Israel receives laws on purification after childbirth.
Leviticus 13: At Sinai, the priests receive instructions for examining skin diseases and mold.
Leviticus 14: The laws look ahead to houses in Canaan: "When ye be come into the land of Canaan" (Leviticus 14:34).
Leviticus 15: At Sinai, Israel receives laws on bodily discharges and uncleanness.
Leviticus 16: The Day of Atonement falls on the tenth day of the seventh month, in autumn (Leviticus 16:29). These rules come at Sinai "after the death of the two sons of Aaron" (Leviticus 16:1).
Leviticus 17: Israel is still living in a camp (Leviticus 17:3), and all sacrifices must be brought to the tabernacle.
Leviticus 18: The laws contrast Israel with "the land of Egypt, wherein ye dwelt" and "the land of Canaan, whither I bring you" (Leviticus 18:3).
Leviticus 19: At Sinai, Israel receives laws for holy living, including care for the poor at harvest.
Leviticus 20: At Sinai, Israel receives penalties for Molech worship and other offenses.
Leviticus 21: At Sinai, the priests receive rules on mourning, marriage, and physical fitness for service.
Leviticus 22: At Sinai, the priests receive rules for eating holy food and accepting sacrifices.
Leviticus 23: Israel's yearly calendar of sabbath and feasts runs from Passover in spring to tabernacles in autumn.
Leviticus 24: A man who blasphemes is stoned outside the camp (Leviticus 24:23).
Leviticus 25: God gives Moses the sabbath year and jubilee laws "in mount Sinai" (Leviticus 25:1), for when Israel will own land in Canaan.
Leviticus 26: Israel is still camped at Mount Sinai, about a year after leaving Egypt, as the laws of Leviticus come to a close (Leviticus 26:46).
Leviticus 27: The book ends at Sinai with laws on vows and tithes (Leviticus 27:34).
Numbers 1: The census is taken "in the wilderness of Sinai" on the first day of the second month of the second year (Numbers 1:1), a month after the tabernacle was set up.
Numbers 2: The tribes camp around the tabernacle by their standards, three on each side.
Numbers 3: The Levites are counted "in the wilderness of Sinai" (Numbers 3:14), in the second month of the second year after leaving Egypt (Numbers 1:1).
Numbers 4: Still at Sinai, the Levites are counted for the work of carrying the tabernacle whenever the camp moves.
Numbers 5: At Sinai, Moses receives laws for keeping the camp clean and for the jealousy ordeal.
Numbers 6: At Sinai, Moses receives the Nazarite vow and the priestly blessing.
Numbers 7: This chapter goes back to "the day that Moses had fully set up the tabernacle" (Numbers 7:1), a month before the census in chapter 1.
Numbers 8: The Levites are purified and set apart; they serve from age twenty-five to fifty (Numbers 8:24–25).
Numbers 9: Israel keeps Passover in the wilderness of Sinai in the first month of the second year (Numbers 9:1).
Numbers 10: Israel leaves Sinai on the twentieth day of the second month of the second year (Numbers 10:11) for the wilderness of Paran.
Numbers 11: At Taberah and Kibrothhattaavah, the people complain about manna and God sends quails.
Numbers 12: At Hazeroth, Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses.
Numbers 13: The twelve spies are sent from the wilderness of Paran and return after forty days to Kadesh (Numbers 13:25–26), in the northern Sinai.
Numbers 14: Israel is camped at Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran, on the edge of Canaan, just after the spies return (Numbers 13:26).
Numbers 15: These laws are given in the wilderness after the refusal at Kadesh. The text does not say exactly when.
Numbers 16: This rebellion happens during the years of wandering in the wilderness. The text gives no date or place.
Numbers 17: Right after Korah's rebellion and the plague, at the tabernacle in the wilderness camp (Numbers 16:49–50).
Numbers 18: Still in the wilderness, after Korah's rebellion has shown the danger of coming near the tabernacle (Numbers 17:12–13).
Numbers 19: In the wilderness years, after many have died in Korah's rebellion and the plague that followed (Numbers 16:49).
Numbers 20: In the first month, Israel is back at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin. Miriam dies there and Aaron dies on mount Hor (Numbers 20:1, 28), in the fortieth year (Numbers 33:38).
Numbers 21: In the fortieth year, Israel travels from mount Hor around Edom and north to the plains of Moab (Numbers 21:4; Numbers 22:1).
Numbers 22: Israel camps "in the plains of Moab on this side Jordan by Jericho" (Numbers 22:1). Balak king of Moab sends for Balaam from Pethor by the Euphrates.
Numbers 23: Balaam speaks from the heights overlooking Israel's camp in the plains of Moab.
Numbers 24: Balak takes Balaam to "the top of Peor, that looketh toward Jeshimon" (Numbers 23:28), above Israel's camp in the plains of Moab.
Numbers 25: At Shittim in the plains of Moab, Israel joins in the worship of Baalpeor.
Numbers 26: A second census is taken in the plains of Moab. None of those counted at Sinai is left except Caleb and Joshua (Numbers 26:64–65).
Numbers 27: Israel is camped in the plains of Moab in the fortieth year, near the end of Moses' life (Numbers 26:3; Numbers 27:12–13).
Numbers 28: In the plains of Moab, Moses receives the schedule of daily, sabbath, monthly, and feast offerings.
Numbers 29: Still in the plains of Moab, Moses gives the offerings for the feasts of the seventh month, in autumn.
Numbers 30: In the plains of Moab, Moses receives laws on vows made by men and women.
Numbers 31: From the camp in the plains of Moab, Israel sends its army against Midian in Moses' last campaign (Numbers 31:2).
Numbers 32: Israel is camped in the plains of Moab, beside the land of Jazer and Gilead it has just conquered (Numbers 32:1).
Numbers 33: The list covers the whole forty years, from Rameses "on the fifteenth day of the first month" to the plains of Moab (Numbers 33:3; Numbers 33:48).
Numbers 34: Moses speaks in the plains of Moab, with Canaan just across the Jordan.
Numbers 35: In the plains of Moab "by Jordan near Jericho" (Numbers 35:1), as Israel gets ready to divide the land.
Numbers 36: The book ends in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho (Numbers 36:13).
